floor_history.headline: Recon: floor 25 -> 14 in pure C (cheat scaffold dropped, worth 0); residual is now register-name-only, 136 vs 136 insns, in exactly two clusters.
Floor 14 -> 8: moving `i = 0;` inside the loop guard closed the whole callee-save cluster; both session-1 frontier mechanisms measured dead and replaced with instrumented successors.

frontier.hypothesis: The 2-point delay-slot residue: target's `i = 0;` sits before the rand() call (proven from reorg.c's call-slot filling rules), yet the counter still takes $s0 there. A C shape exists that gets both; the discriminator is in local-alloc, not global alloc.
frontier.mechanism: global.c is measured inert for this flip (identical allocno tables across the 14/8 forms), so the $s0/$s1 choice is made by local-alloc.c quantity assignment - most likely qty_phys_sugg / suggested-register propagation - or by reload.
frontier.next_probe: FORENSICS modality. Run the instrumented cc1 with BB2_QTY_DEBUG (local-alloc.c:1518/1585) and BB2_SUGG_DEBUG (local-alloc.c:1437/1447/2215) on memory/grind/func_800174F4/candidate.c vs memory/grind/func_800174F4/rejected/i-init-before-call.c (reuse tmp/grind/func_800174F4/s2/dump.sh, which already sets up the exact cc1 flags), and read which quantity is handed $s0 and on what suggestion. Then look for a C shape that reproduces the winning suggestion with a pre-call initialisation.

frontier.hypothesis: Cluster (A), 6 pts: the switch selector reaches $a1 only if its allocno conflicts with whatever holds $v0, $v1 and $a0, because no copy preference can survive combine (K6) and MIPS has no REG_ALLOC_ORDER override.
frontier.mechanism: global.c:find_reg allocates the lowest-numbered non-conflicting register of the class; the selector is allocated 2nd overall and currently conflicts only with the $v0 holder.
frontier.next_probe: First VERIFY the conflict hypothesis: take a cc1 `-dg` dump of the floor-8 form and read the selector allocno's conflict list out of the `.greg` output. If regs 2/3/4 are already in its conflict set the hypothesis is wrong and cluster (A) is also a local-alloc question. If not, search for an honest C shape in which the dispatch value is still live across the func_8005D46C call region (target insns 43-45) so it conflicts with the $a0 argument pseudo and the $v1 g_disp_fade pseudo at once.

frontier.hypothesis: A directed permuter campaign from the floor-8 base closes the register-name residual.
frontier.mechanism: The residual is a clean 136-vs-136 register-name-only diff in two small clusters, which is the shape decomp-permuter's weighted register scoring searches well; the base is now 6 points closer than the one session 1 proposed seeding from.
frontier.next_probe: Build a single-function target.o from asm/funcs/func_800174F4.s + tools/decomp-permuter/prelude.inc (drop `.set gp=64`) per .claude/rules/difficult-is-not-impossible.md so the base score is the real weighted diff, seed from memory/grind/func_800174F4/candidate.c, and run a fresh-seed campaign via tools/permuter_campaign.py - launching, waiting (`wait --dir <ws>`) and `harvest --stop` all inside the same turn.
